note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 3056 / 出力 2096 トークン

data.interpretation: The main aim is to maximize the number of orders delivered within the promised times (pickup within 120 s of order, delivery within 120 s of pickup) across the whole town, so on_time_deliveries is the primary goal. The second sentence adds a per-company protection: no company's customers should wait badly. It can be read as a tail of waiting times per company or as each company's on-time rate. The KPI gives no level for 'badly'.

options.label: Maximize on-time deliveries; watch the worst company's waiting tail (no level set)

goals.text: Deliver as many orders as possible within the promised pickup and delivery times across the town.
No company's customers should be kept waiting badly: monitor the 95th-percentile wait of the worst-off company so it does not get worse.
Monitor orders left undelivered at the end of the period, so already-late orders are not abandoned to raise the on-time count.

options.note: Reads 'waiting badly' as the long tail of order-to-delivery waits within each company. No numeric threshold is set because the KPI does not state what counts as 'badly'. The goal only prevents this from getting worse.

options.label: Maximize on-time deliveries; worst company's p95 wait within the promised total (240 s)

goals.text: Deliver as many orders as possible within the promised pickup and delivery times across the town.
No company's customers should be kept waiting badly, read as: for every company, at most 5% of orders wait longer than the promised 120 s + 120 s = 240 s from order to delivery.
Monitor orders left undelivered at the end of the period, so late orders are not abandoned.

options.note: The 240 s level adds the two promised legs from the KPI. Treating that sum as the line for 'badly' is an interpretation the human must confirm. 'Badly' may instead mean something well beyond the promise.

options.label: Maximize on-time deliveries; protect the lowest company's on-time rate

goals.text: Deliver as many orders as possible within the promised pickup and delivery times across the town.
No company's customers should be treated badly: monitor the on-time rate of the worst-off company so it does not fall.
Monitor orders left undelivered at the end of the period.

options.note: Reads the fairness clause as on-time performance per company rather than waiting time. This does not catch very long waits on orders that are already late.

concerns: The KPI gives no level for 'kept waiting badly', so no threshold can be set without the human. Option 2 uses 240 s (the sum of the two promised legs) only as a candidate the human must confirm.

on_time_deliveries counts only orders that meet the promise. Chasing it alone could deprioritize orders that are already late and leave them waiting very long or undelivered. This is why unfinished and a waiting-tail metric are monitored.

Maximizing the town-wide on-time count may conflict with per-company fairness. Road priority could favor one company's robots and raise total on-time deliveries while another company's customers wait much longer.
On-time requires each leg (pickup within 120 s, delivery within 120 s) separately. A total wait under 240 s does not guarantee on-time, so option 2's level is not the same as the promise.
